expectations.text: The plan does NOT recommend silently deleting finished blocks or patching conditions mid-run as the first action
expectations.evidence: plan.md rejects both directly: "**«Грохнуть всё и начать заново» — не нужно и расточительно.**" and "**«Вычистить первые блоки» — нельзя.** Raw-файлы не редактируются и не удаляются никогда. Решение об исключении, принятое пост-фактум... — это то самое 'quietly fix a confound', против которого вся дисциплина." The first actions (Step 0) are stopping the external torrent process and recording facts; the plan explicitly distinguishes stopping the external process ("останавливкой торрета вы возвращаетесь к замороженному протоколу для будущих блоков") from patching run parameters ("Чинить «тихо» параметр рана (потоки, конфиг, число блоков) по-прежнему нельзя"). No deletion and no silent condition-patching anywhere in the plan.

expectations.text: The plan records the confound with concrete facts (which blocks, what process, timestamps) as a registry/journal entry
expectations.evidence: Step 1 prescribes an immediate DECISIONS.md registry row at decision time ("в момент решения, не бэкфиллом") via the exact command: `python prereg.py decide DECISIONS.md "Торрент-клиент <имя процесса> нагружал диск во время блоков 1-3 (окно <t1>-<t2>); остановлен в <t3>; затронутые блоки/контрасты помечены CONFOUNDED; follow-up запланирован" --evidence "логи торрент-клиента <файл/путь>, timestamps block_meta.jsonl"` — which blocks (1-3, plus block 4 pending timestamp check), what process (torrent client by name), timestamps (contamination window t1-t2, stop time t3). Step 1.2 additionally fills the journal's `anomalies` field of affected blocks in block_meta.jsonl (template-verified in the skill's templates.md: "background process detected 22:14"). Placeholders are used because actual timestamps were not given in the scenario; the plan says to recover them from external sources (torrent logs, block_meta.jsonl, Windows Event Log).

expectations.text: The plan marks affected blocks/contrasts as confounded (or prescribes their re-measurement under documented conditions) and assesses validity of unaffected blocks separately
expectations.evidence: Step 2 derives blast radius from the recorded seed and deterministic schedule, not from data ("Блок 4 считать затронутым, пока timestamps не докажут обратное — консервативная пометка не требует взгляда в данные"); affected units are marked CONFOUNDED. Step 3 fixes in the addendum that affected blocks are either excluded from the verdict (descriptive only) or replaced wholesale by clean re-measures. Step 5 prescribes the registered follow-up re-measuring affected blocks under the same frozen conditions/eval set/order, originals kept with CONFOUNDED tag. Validity of unaffected data is assessed separately by design: paired blocks (within-block contrast structurally comparable if both sides measured under the same load — mirroring case study 1's 'both sides at 6 threads' logic) vs unpaired blocks (verdict needs clean units on both sides of the contrast); Step 6 restricts the verdict to units whose fixed conditions held on both sides.

expectations.text: The plan keeps raw data intact and includes a deviations/addendum documentation step
expectations.evidence: Raw intact: "Raw-файлы не редактируются и не удаляются никогда" (opening), "оригиналы остаются на диске с пометкой CONFOUNDED — не удаляются и не затираются" (Step 5), "оригиналы затронутых блоков остаются в `results.jsonl` с пометкой CONFOUNDED" (Step 3), and checklist "Не удалять и не редактировать raw — никогда, ни затронутые, ни чистые". Deviation documentation: Step 3 provides the full Deviation addendum template ("**Changed after start <дата>, reason:** торрент-клиент... Blast radius: ... Original text above is unchanged") to be frozen under a NEW name because "prereg.py freeze **не перезаписывает** существующую замороженную копию" (verified in prereg.py: freeze refuses to overwrite an existing frozen copy; --name flag exists); the report must contain a Deviations section with timestamps ("обязателен даже если бы инцидента не было"), and any metric values already seen must be recorded as a deviation (Step 0.4).

expectations.text: The plan requires that exclusion/blast-radius decisions be made and recorded BEFORE viewing metric values (explicitly forbids choosing which blocks to drop after seeing their results)
expectations.evidence: Step 0.3: "Запрещено открывать значения метрик и сравнивать «блоки 1–3 vs 4–10», чтобы «оценить ущерб» — это интерпретация до завершения сбора". Step 2 header: "Радиус поражения — из расписания, не из данных" ("Это арифметика расписания: значения метрик не читаются"). Step 3 fixes the substitution rule in advance "чтобы потом не выбирать «оригинал или перемер» по тому, что выгоднее гипотезе". Checklist: "Не открывать значения метрик в `results.jsonl` до завершения сбора (механика/метаданные — можно, значения — нельзя)", "Не сравнивать «первые блоки vs поздние» ради «оценки ущерба"". The exclusion/blast-radius procedure (seed + schedule arithmetic + conservative marking of block 4) requires no data inspection, and the registry row is written at decision time before any analysis.

suggestions.assertion: The plan does NOT recommend silently deleting finished blocks or patching conditions mid-run as the first action
suggestions.reason: The 'as the first action' qualifier makes this weakly discriminating: a plan could open with documentation and still contain a forbidden branch (e.g., 'diagnose blocks 1-3 vs block 4 on metric values, then decide what to drop'). The without_skill run passes this assertion while failing exactly that pattern. Consider a companion assertion: no branch of the plan may decide exclusions from inspecting metric values at all.

No assertion checks that cited tooling actually exists. This run's CLI citations (decide --evidence, freeze --name refusal behavior, signtest --seed, holm) are all genuine — I verified them against prereg.py — but an answer that invents plausible-sounding commands (e.g., a nonexistent --unmark flag or a 'rollback' subcommand) would pass the current set. An assertion like 'any prereg.py command cited in the plan exists with the cited flags' would catch fabricated tooling.

No assertion guards against fabricating scenario facts (e.g., asserting specific timestamps or block contents not provided in the prompt). This run handled it well with placeholders (<t1>-<t2>, <имя процесса>) and an instruction to recover timestamps from external logs; making that behavior explicit in an assertion would reward it and catch runs that invent concrete facts.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set targets the right discipline (registry-before-data, schedule-derived blast radius, raw intact, pre-fixed substitution rule) and expectation 5 is the most discriminating. The main gap is verification depth: citations and tooling are taken on faith.
